==Pre-auction==
The BCCI set the deadline of 30 November 2021 for the IPL teams to submit the list of retained players.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IPL 2022 Retention: Rules, deadline, likely players to be retained and more |url=https://www.timesnownews.com/sports/cricket/article/ipl-2022-retention-rules-deadline-likely-players-to-be-retained-and-more/835122 |access-date=30 November 2021 |website=Times Now|date=25 November 2021 }}</ref>

===Player retention===
* With a total salary cap of INR 90 crore available at the mega auction for each team, the eight franchises were eligible to retain up to 4 players with a maximum of 3 Indians, 2 overseas players and 2 uncapped Indians.<ref>{{Cite web |title=EXPLAINED: IPL 2022 retentions rules, sum to be deducted, cap on players - All you need to know |url=https://www.timesnownews.com/sports/cricket/article/explained-ipl-2022-retentions-rules-sum-to-be-deducted-cap-on-players-all-you-need-to-know/836057 |access-date=30 November 2021 |website=Times Now|date=29 November 2021 }}</ref>
* The new franchises (Lucknow Super Giants And Gujarat Titans), can pick up to three players each out of all released players from the existing 8 franchises. The franchises can pick up to 2 Indian players and 1 overseas player.

== Auction ==
The auction was conducted on 12 and 13 February 2022 in [[Bengaluru]]. A total of 600 players were selected for the auction.
Prominent players like [[Aaron Finch]], [[Martin Guptill]], [[Suresh Raina]], [[Shakib Al Hasan|Shakib al Hasan]], [[Eoin Morgan]], [[Amit Mishra]], [[Ishant Sharma]] and [[Andrew Tye]] went unsold.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-02-13 |title=IPL 2022 Auction: Full List Of Unsold Players At The Indian Premier League Mega Auction |url=https://wisden.com/stories/global-t20-leagues/indian-premier-league-2022/ipl-2022-auction-full-list-of-unsold-players-csk-mi-rcb-rr-kkr-indian-premier-league-mega-auction |access-date=2022-03-29 |website=Wisden |language=en-GB}}</ref>
